P3 kitchen-dining furnished in parts/room-21.mjs: dining table (spruce legs, top slabs) on the west side, lit stove on the hearth wall facing the doorway, a stool, a barrel with a flower pot, and two hanging lanterns.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the part places 12 blocks with no refused writes or off-palette blocks. Room check: FIT OK, light min 11 with 0 dark cells.
The walk verdict reads "no way in" only because the front door, stair hall and stair joiner are unbuilt in this copy; my lanes are unverified until they exist.
left: Walkability not verified end to end: the room check says no way in until the front door, the P3 stair hall and the stair joiner exist in the merged build. Re-run `$MCD room ... --only "P3 kitchen-dining"` after the merge; the lane (42,14)-(43,14)-(42,15) and (41,14) should then read reachable.

The stool at (42,15) and the stove's front cell (41,14) are the only spots to stand by the stove and table; there is no seating across the table because the 2-wide room leaves no lane if a chair sits on (41,14).
Structure warnings in the whole build are outside this part: floating stairs at x54, x88, x91 (stair joiner flights not yet built) and an unsupported ladder at 62,1,14 (barn part).
plan.md has no checklist item for this room and elements.md has none for the kitchen-dining interior, so nothing was ticked.

waste.what: table_set() lays its top as a BOTTOM slab, so the first build put a flower pot floating over air; I rebuilt the table by hand with g.set() top slabs.
waste.cost: one make.sh + room + fit cycle (about 1 minute), plus two rebuilds of the table layout
waste.tool: table_set() should take a top-slab option (or default to type top), as the furnisher's rule says tables are top slabs; the fit check already catches it but the helper should not produce it.

waste.what: Judged which cells stay free by hand (doorway first cells, stove front, table stand) across the 2x4 room, working the lane out cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 4 layouts sketched in my head; one chair moved after the walk check flagged the table as blocked
waste.tool: a layout check in `mcd room` that names which furniture cell blocks the stand cell of a table or stove (it currently reports only unreachable floor), plus a stand-cell option in the plan grid.

waste.what: The walk verdict cannot be checked for this room while the entrance chain is unbuilt, so reachability inside the room is only inferred from the floor grid.
waste.cost: no retries; left as an open check for after the merge
waste.tool: `mcd room --from-plan` or a stub-entrance option that treats an unbuilt doorway as open, so the room's own lanes can be verified in isolation.

waste.what: Placed the barrel, its flower pot and the table pot with separate g.set() calls instead of a short layers() grid.
waste.tool: Negligible here; a small `dresser`-style helper with a pot on top would cover it.
